title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Free-Probability Certificates for Sparse Random Hamiltonians, Non-Crossing Cumulant Bijections, and Spiked Spectral Phase Transitions
abstract: Ding, King, and Schuster (arXiv:2611.33128, November 24, 2026) introduced classical algorithms for estimating the density of states, thermal expectation values, and spectral phase transitions of sparse random n-qubit Pauli Hamiltonians H = m^(-1/2) sum J_i P_i via non-crossing free-cumulant resummation in time poly(1/eps) independent of system size n. We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formal verification and certificate auditing framework for the finite-order algebraic backbone of this paradigm. First, we formalize an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (FreeProbHamiltonians.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 5 zero-axiom theorems) covering exact Catalan semicircle moments, inductive Catalan positivity, order-4/6/8 non-crossing moment-cumulant inversion, symmetric Bernoulli spike free cumulants, exact free-additive critical-cusp moments at lambda = 1, binary symplectic Pauli commutation algebra, universal sparse fourth-cumulant brackets -m^2 <= m^2 k4 <= m^2 - 2m, exponential decay monotonicity (Ck)^r < m^r, inductive list truncation tail bounds, and the exact precision separation (2^b)^2 < 2^n. Second, we introduce FREE-PROB-HAM-CERT-1.0 and a pure-stdlib zero-float verifier spanning four modes: 4-loop-free sparse Pauli exact (m2, m4, k4) verification via O(m^2) symplectic XOR collision detection, exact NC(2r) moment-cumulant bijection up to order 20, exact spiked-Pauli phase-transition certification across subcritical/critical/supercritical regimes, and cumulant-truncation tail and (1/eps)^2 < 2^n barrier audits. Across 16 canonical certificates, zero-float replay runs in 0.067-2.890 ms, matches direct 2^n x 2^n matrix traces Tr(H^4)/2^n, and rejects 54/54 live adversarial forgeries.
